entry_points.text: Mq open validates name and creates or opens backing file with mode and attrs; unlink resolves under mount root with write protection and pinned inode across filesystem unlink.
Native timed send and receive translate optional absolute timeout or use null deadline then call internal workers; 32-bit variants translate old layout with EFAULT and EINVAL on failure.
Notify and attr native paths copy user blocks and delegate with null as disarm; compat paths translate narrow attrs and sigevent with cookie adjustment and paired converters in both directions.

Msgget resolves ns and delegates to generic get; msgctl validates ids and dispatches info, stat, set and remove with version selector; legacy parses version bit; sighand acquire returns null when detached.

exports.text: Pending-signal accounting across user namespaces with null on failure, jobctl pending and trapping helpers with consume and ordered wakeup, plus sighand acquisition and payload layout classification.
Identity translation for user and group ids with munged overflow fallback, extent range lookup, and group membership test against fs group plus supplementary list.
Chained message alloc and user copy helpers with security hook and fault cleanup, compat sigevent fetch, private mq mount setup with defaults, and queue removal forwarding.
System V identifier alloc with stamped identities and hashed keys, private versus public get dispatch, permission and control checks, perm translation, version parse, and RCU reference release.

hazards.text: Non-queueing alloc failure marks delivery but drops origin detail; ucount guards overflow and underflow with warnings; sighand reuse handled by stable alloc and revalidate; limit exhaustion gated and rate-limited; traced fatal withheld except SIGKILL. Constants: SIGRTMIN, SEND_SIG_NOINFO, SEND_SIG_PRIV, SI_USER, SI_KERNEL, SI_TIMER, SI_SIGIO, SIGCONT, SIG_KERNEL_STOP_MASK, JOBCTL bits, UCOUNT_RLIMIT_SIGPENDING.

Mq failures map to EFAULT, EBADF, EMSGSIZE, EINVAL, EAGAIN, EBUSY, ENOMEM with netlink errors propagated; spare leaves only fill empty cache; messages freed on insert, sleep or copy faults; cookies and sockets cleaned; unlink pins inode. Selection codes any1 equal2 notequal3 lessequal4 numeric5; compat reserves four zeroed slots.

Objects visible at publication must be fully initialized with full teardown on failure; wakeups collected under guard and delivered after release; receiver result needs release pairing. Sequence shift has two build variants with max derived; version tags select 64-bit or old layout with saturated plus extended counters.

External helpers for locks, RCU, atomics, barriers, lists, idr, copy, audit, security, files, time and alloc are owned elsewhere and only referenced here; no behavior specified for them in this dossier.

invariants.text: Group deliveries use shared pending and private use per-task pending; standard pending coalesce; SIGKILL and kthreads skip info alloc; alloc failure gives EAGAIN on queueing paths else marks with info loss.

Blocked never ignored and traced observed except SIGKILL; init, unkillable and kthread rules honored; exiting groups drop except SIGKILL in coredump; stop and continue purge each other and wake or notify.
Wake eligibility needs unblocked, non-exiting, responsive or SIGKILL, and running or no pending; fatal unblocked starts group exit and wakes; hinted thread preferred then round-robin scan.
Upward id lookup needs full containment in one extent, linear for compact and ordered for large maps; uncovered yields sentinel mapped to overflow by munged wrapper.

Mq validates prio, descriptor, mode, length and buffer size; full or empty sleeps or EAGAIN; direct handoff or insert with notify; notify allows three modes with owner checks; attr only toggles nonblock.

Id low bits index and high bits sequence with EINVAL on absent or mismatch; teardown removes slot and hash, updates max by downward probe; ns zeroes counts and installs defaults; alloc chains leading plus segments.

New queue zeroes usage with ns default capacity and empty lists; send needs byte and count fit; idr reuses cyclically with sequence wrap; old status saturates 16-bit plus full fields; validity is deletion flag clear.

locks.text: Sighand ownership for queue mutation, flush, exit checks and traps; IRQ-safe acquire with revalidate and retry on detach; RCU for creds and ucounts; barriers for extents and trapping wakeup.

Per-inode mq lock guards attrs, spare cache, waiter lists and notify; readiness published under lock with deferred wakeups after unlock; file flag lock nests inside; unlink uses mount write protection.

Object spin guard plus RCU read lock returned held by alloc and lookup; set write guard for create and public lookup, read guard for info; control holds write plus read plus object with wakeups after object unlock.

state_machines.text: Jobctl moves among pending, consumed and dequeued with trapping wakeup and seized-trap notify; continue records stopped versus interrupted stop; timers use ignored versus free paths; generation reports ignored, pending, delivered, overflow or info-loss.

Mq open goes lookup, create-or-open with audit and perms, file instantiate and descriptor with write-hold cleanup; waiters sleep in none state then adopt or free; direct handoff dequeues, refs task and defers wakeup.

Senders enqueue interruptible, cancel if linked, wake scan rotates unfit and queues fit or force-kills all; receivers abort with encoded error; teardown aborts both, delivers wakeups, frees messages and drops to RCU free; control either removes or updates perm and capacity.

structs.text: Queued node links into pending list with flags, accounting ref and origin info; pending pairs mask plus list, shared for group and per-task for private; id map uses inline or ordered extents.
SysV queue embeds perm header plus stamps, byte and count usage, capacity, last pids and three lists; waiter records hold task, size or result pointer; layout randomized.

Compat mq attrs hold flags, max count, max size, current count plus four reserved slots; mq fs wires fixed dir, file, super, context and type tables; id set holds guards, usage, indexes, tree and hash.
